Accede

/ak-SEED/ - rhymes with succeed · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Accede means to agree to a request or proposal.

After a year of petitions about the dangerous school corner, the city acceded and painted the crosswalk over spring break.

Worked Example

Her grandmother had said no to a kitten for years — too much fur, too much noise. When the twins presented a chore chart and a vet-fund jar, she studied both, sighed, and acceded; there was a kitten in the house by Friday.

Accede is sharper than plain 'agree' because it marks the moment a holdout gives way: you can only accede to something asked of you, and the word quietly reports that you were resisting it first.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

assent: Assent is formal agreement that a statement, plan, or opinion is sound — a nod of approval in a boardroom. You assent to ideas; you accede to requests made of you, and accede adds what assent never carries: the sense that you resisted before finally giving way.

agree: Agree is the plain, everyday word for any shared yes — you can agree with a friend, a plan, or a forecast, instantly and gladly. Accede is narrower and more formal: it answers a request or demand aimed at you, and it reports that you held out first.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

refuse: to say no outright

resist: to keep pushing back rather than give way

Where it sits · how much yielding the agreement involves — consider → consent → accede

consider vs. accede: To consider a request is much milder than to accede to it — considering only weighs the ask, while accede means the resistance ended and the thing asked for was granted.

consent vs. accede: Consent stops short of accede — you can consent gladly on the spot, while accede means a holdout finally gave way.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ac-

Prefix — ac-: to, toward (a form of ad-)

Root — ced-

Root — ced-: to go, to yield

Put it together

Put it together: Ac- (to, toward) + ced- (to go, yield) = to go along toward what is asked. Latin accedere meant 'to approach, to join a side' — when you accede, you finally walk over to the asking side. The same ced- root runs through this unit's concede and through recede, precede, and exceed.

Use the root in a new word: recede

Use the root in a new word: recede: By morning the floodwater had receded, going back down the lane it came up.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Accede is formal and always points at someone else's request, demand, or proposal — you accede to it, usually after holding out. For everyday yeses, agree or consent is plainer. Its unit-mates pull differently: acquiesce stresses reluctant silence, and concede means granting a point in an argument.
